title: Emergency Medical Triage System
business: Emergency room intake departments managing patient flow.
problem: Standard first-come, first-served queues cause critical patients to wait behind minor cases, leading to preventable health deterioration.
solution: A priority queue implementation allows the system to organize patients by clinical urgency (triage level) rather than arrival time, ensuring the highest-acuity patients are processed first.
steps: Assign a numerical priority score to each patient upon intake.
Insert patient records into a binary heap structure based on their score.
Extract the patient with the highest priority score for the next available physician.
Maintain the heap property after each extraction to ensure the next most urgent patient is at the root.
outcome: Improved patient safety and reduced wait times for critical cases.
limitation: The primary limitation is that low-priority patients may suffer from 'starvation' if high-priority patients continue to arrive, which can be checked by monitoring the maximum wait time of the lowest-priority records.

questions.question: In Emergency Medical Triage System, why is a priority queue preferred over a standard queue?
options: It ensures critical patients are processed before minor cases.
It reduces the total number of patients entering the hospital.
It allows for faster registration of patient insurance data.
It automatically assigns doctors to patients based on specialty.
questions.explanation: The business problem is that standard queues cause critical patients to wait behind minor cases; a priority queue solves this by ordering by urgency.
questions.evidence: A priority queue implementation allows the system to organize patients by clinical urgency (triage level) rather than arrival time, ensuring the highest-acuity patients are processed first.

questions.question: In Emergency Medical Triage System, what is a potential risk of using a priority queue?
options: The system might run out of memory for patient records.
The doctors will work too quickly for the system.
The priority scores might become too large to store.
questions.explanation: Priority queues can cause starvation for low-priority items if high-priority items are constantly added, which is a known limitation.
questions.evidence: The primary limitation is that low-priority patients may suffer from 'starvation' if high-priority patients continue to arrive, which can be checked by monitoring the maximum wait time of the lowest-priority records.
